stories.title: Chief Justice temporarily allows Trump ballroom work to continue
new_facts: Supreme Court temporarily allows $400M White House ballroom construction to continue pending final ruling.
Names Chief Justice John Roberts as the one issuing the stay.
Reveals Ed Martin, a Trump ally pushing election fraud claims, is leaving the administration to help with midterms.
Ballroom project is now 90,000 square feet and tied to renovation of an underground military bunker, per Trump's lawyers.
Lower court injunction was set to halt construction within hours; courts had found Trump could not unilaterally demolish White House sections.
stories.line: Chief Justice Roberts temporarily allows Trump administration to continue ballroom renovation work pending further legal review.

stories.title: Trump waives beef tariffs for 90 days ahead of midterms
new_facts: Beef prices soared in 2026 due to a reduced US cattle herd, prompting the tariff exemption.
Trump to temporarily allow more beef imports without higher tariffs to lower prices; some Republicans object.
Trump exempts 300,000 metric tons of imported ground beef from tariffs ahead of midterms.
stories.line: Trump temporarily waives tariffs on 300,000 metric tons of imported ground beef to reduce prices before the midterm elections.

stories.title: Salmonella and E. coli outbreak from alfalfa sprouts spreads to 15 states
new_facts: New story: salmonella/E. coli outbreak linked to alfalfa sprouts spreads to 15 states, 55 cases, 4 hospitalized.
stories.line: Salmonella and E. coli outbreak linked to alfalfa sprouts has sickened at least 55 people across 15 states.

stories.title: White House sets 1,000 annual rocket launches as space policy target
new_facts: Trump signed new national space policy targeting 1,000+ rocket launches per year by 2030.
Policy also includes working with commercial space industry to send humans to Mars.
Policy targets 3 launches per day and directs expansion of launch pads, airspace corridors and air traffic control.
stories.line: Trump administration sets target of 1,000 annual rocket launches by 2030, a roughly 10-fold increase from current pace.

stories.title: Schools adopt phone bans, open new buildings as year begins
stories.line: Michigan and Maryland schools implement new policies: cell phone restrictions and fitness assessments in Michigan; new school buildings open in Montgomery County.

stories.title: Russian drone strikes kill civilians at Ukrainian shopping center
new_facts: Establishes attack: 15 killed in double-tap drone strike on mall in Zelenskyy's hometown.
Adds injury count of over 100 and names city Kryvyi Rih.
Adds injury toll of 130, including 23 children, per regional head.
Reports death toll of six and injuries of 103, differing from earlier 15 killed.
Reports 14 killed, over 120 injured, and new Zelenskyy quote calling attack 'cynical and despicable'.
Adds detail that second drone struck about 30 minutes after the first, per Zelensky.
Reports six killed, about 90 injured, including six children — new injury/child figures.
stories.line: Russian drone strikes hit a shopping center in Ukraine, killing at least six to fifteen civilians depending on source.

stories.title: Supreme Court temporarily allows Trump White House ballroom construction
new_facts: SCOTUS allows $400M ballroom construction to continue; administration cites national security justification
Names National Trust for Historic Preservation as plaintiff challenging construction for months
Notes East Wing was demolished in 2025 to make way for the ballroom
Reports a midnight deadline for the Supreme Court to rule on the ballroom case
Op-ed by Trump's former National Security Advisor argues ballroom is urgent national security/safety matter
stories.line: Supreme Court temporarily allows Trump's ballroom construction at the White House to proceed while legal challenges continue.

stories.title: One killed, several injured in sword attack at Swedish school
new_facts: Adds attacker's age (18) and casualty breakdown: one dead, two injured.
Confirms police arrested the attacker, resolving earlier arrested-vs-shot ambiguity.
Names the school as Brinell School in Fagersta.
New story: sword-wielding attacker wounds several people at a school in Sweden
Names location as Fagersta; other schools and public buildings placed in lockdown
stories.line: A person wielding a sword attacked a school in central Sweden, killing one and injuring at least two others.

stories.title: TikTok settles $400M child privacy lawsuit with US Justice Department
new_facts: TikTok reaches $400M settlement with DOJ over alleged COPPA children's privacy violations
stories.line: TikTok will pay $400 million to settle a federal lawsuit alleging it violated child privacy laws by collecting data on minors without proper consent.

stories.title: Trump pardon attorney Ed Martin leaves Justice Department
new_facts: Trump announces Ed Martin is leaving his post as DOJ pardon attorney.
Martin, a 'Stop the Steal' organizer and Jan. 6 defense attorney, leaves to focus on 2026 election legal battles.
stories.line: Trump's pardon attorney Ed Martin is leaving the Justice Department amid upcoming election legal battles.
